newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-WIMBLEDON WASHED OUT FOR SECOND CONSECUTIVE DAY.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-WIMBLEDON WASHED OUT FOR SECOND CONSECUTIVE DAY.

text.p: Unrelenting rain washed out play for the second consecutive day at the Wimbledon championships on Friday with more showers forecast for the weekend.

It was the first time since 1909 that two successive days have been rained out, leaving tournament organisers 260 matches behind schedule. Tuesday has been the only uninterrupted day so far in the first week of the two-week championships.
Officials will decide at 1500GMT on Saturday whether to play on the middle Sunday, usually a rest day, for the second time in the history of the championships.
The men's doubles competition, yet to get underway, has already been reduced to the best of three sets for the first three rounds.
Further rain is likely on Saturday and Sunday with no break predicted until Monday in the depression which has disrupted the English summer sports season.
British number one Tim Henman, the 14th seed, defended Wimbledon traditions and said he did not believe there should be a roof over the only Grand Slam grass court tournament.
"It's an outdoor tournament and it should remain that way," Henman told a news conference.
Henman also said he believed the tournament should stay on grass.
"It's unique in a lot ways and especially that way," Henman said. "It's inevitable you are going to have years when the weather is bad."
The players have been as depressed as the scattering of spectators huddled on the show courts willing the clouds to disappear.
"There's only a certain amount of practices you can have, lunches you can have, games of backgammon you can have," Henman concluded.
Venus Williams, the American teenager who had been due to make her Wimbledon debut on Friday, was more sanguine.
"I'm not frustrated at all," she said. "I think maybe a lot of other players are. But I'm just fine."
